title: The wedding day
hookLine: the couple walks the four lavan round the Granth
tomorrow: four rounds, four stages. which one is a new couple in?

lines: A SCARF FROM FATHER TO DAUGHTER.
cards: Weddings in movies peak at a kiss or a vow. This one peaks at a walk. The darbar hall is full and the shoes are piled at the door.
Jasleen sits beside Aman in front of the Guru Granth Sahib, both in red.
Chacha Balwinder, three days retired, leans down and places one end of a long scarf in his daughter's hand; the other end is already over Aman's shoulder. The ragis start to sing.
And Aman stands up, and Jasleen follows, and they begin to walk.

teach.h: ANAND KARAJ: THE CEREMONY OF BLISS.
teach.b: The Sikh wedding is the Anand Karaj, the ceremony of bliss, and at its heart are the lavan: four verses by Guru Ram Das, on ang 773 and 774.
Each verse is read from the Granth, then sung while the couple walks once around it, the groom ahead, the bride behind, joined by the palla, that scarf.

teach.h: THE PALLA JOINS THEM, ROUND THE GRANTH.
teach.b: Nothing is signed at the center, nobody exchanges rings at the Granth; the walking is the wedding.
And the week walks with them. Bebe's daswandh envelope, carried to the pantry shelf: give wisely. Harjit's Japji line in the group chat: gift, not ranking.
Aman's fifteen-minute meeting: rise anyway. Chacha's ladle: keep serving. Bebe's three columns: earn, share, remember.
Jasleen's henna and her straight answer: character first. Simran watches from the third row, one hand on Fateh's shoulder so he stays sitting.
On the fourth round the sangat rises a little in their seats, the way people lean in for the end of a song.

how: At an Anand Karaj, each of the four lavan is read from the Guru Granth Sahib and then sung while the couple walks around it, joined by a scarf; Ardas, a hukam and karah prashad follow.

games.q: a friend at her first Sikh wedding whispers: 'when do they actually get married?' the couple is on their second round. what do you whisper back?
o: right now. the four rounds around the Granth are the wedding.

games.why: the Anand Karaj's heart is the lavan: four verses sung as the couple walks round the Guru Granth Sahib.

practice: Listen for one sound around you that keeps going on its own: a fan, traffic, a fridge's hum, birds. Follow just that one sound, round and round, the way the couple circles at a steady pace.
When your mind wanders off, walk it back to that sound.

wordCard.voice: The wedding day. In Sikhi, the Anand Karaj: four lavan, sung as the couple walks round the Guru Granth Sahib.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: lavan, the four wedding verses of Guru Ram Das, and the rounds walked to them.

carryVoice: Four rounds, one scarf, and a whole week walking with them. A full week, done.
